conceptZh: 豬探長追查巨大腳印時撞倒骨牌筆畫，引發連鎖翻倒，把自己彈上最後的踏板，蓋出「獸」字並找出躲在放大鏡後的小怪獸。
object: A giant footprint assembled from hinged, deep-blue stroke dominoes, plus the detective's oversized magnifying glass.
morph: A physical domino cascade folds accurately shaped stroke pieces into 獸; the final falling piece launches the pig onto a pedal that stamps the upper-right dot of 犬.
creativeAngle: 把查腳印變成失控的骨牌機關；末端反彈讓探長親自踩出犬部的點，再揭露放大鏡後的小怪獸，讓字形完成與詞義揭曉接連發生。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized 3D cartoon in one locked, nearly frontal wide shot, with a pale peach floor and warm cream backdrop. Lead: an original stout detective pig, checked deerstalker hat, enormous magnifying glass, boundless confidence and a habit of charging at clues. Use squash-and-stretch animation and soft wooden clacks. One supporting creature: a tiny round mint-green monster with mismatched horns and broad padded feet.

0.00–1.10: The pig spots an enormous footprint made from a compact trail of upright, hinged deep-blue stroke dominoes. He eagerly sights through his magnifier, then lowers his head for a charging investigation. Arrange the dominoes as one simple assembly across the central stage; keep the background empty.

1.10–2.25: He dashes, overshoots the footprint, and catches the first domino with his snout: a tiny BONK, a shocked blink, then the first piece falls. At 1.35 the off-screen voice says “獸” as this physical build begins. The pig scrambles after the falling piece, trying to catch it with the huge lens, and misses.

2.25–4.15: The domino chain accelerates visibly: knock, knock-knock, CLACK! Each falling stroke swings on its hinge and settles flat into its final glyph position, transferring the collision to the next. Use a precise Traditional Chinese 獸 master layout to determine every piece and landing position: preserve the complete left-hand structure, its two distinct upper boxes and lower 口, and the separate right-hand 犬. Keep every counter open and every stroke distinct. These are mechanical stroke pieces, never decorative approximations.

4.15–5.00: The last falling stroke hits a seesaw under the pig: BOING! He flips once and lands bottom-first on a small pedal beside the character. The pedal stamps the final upper-right dot of 犬. At 4.65 the voice says the second “獸” exactly as that dot lands. His soft landing bounces him off the pedal into the lower margin, where he gives a startled thumbs-up.

5.00–8.00: Hold the completed saturated blue 獸 perfectly still, centered, uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. At 5.65 the tiny monster peeks from behind the pig's oversized lens, then plants its comically broad foot beside the footprint trail as the voice says “怪獸”. The delighted pig compares the foot through his lens, wobbles once, and proudly thumbs-up again. Keep both characters below and away from all strokes.

Audio: warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin, exact line “獸、獸、怪獸” (ㄕㄡˋ、ㄕㄡˋ、ㄍㄨㄞˋ ㄕㄡˋ). Read exactly these syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones and short pauses; stop after the word. Gentle effects stay beneath the voice. The single target glyph 獸 is the only visible text; no subtitles, logos, watermark, flashing effects, or extra dialogue.
